deposits.title: THE WAR FOR THE COMPRESSION LAYER A Total Axial Negation Graph
deposits.creator: Johannes Sigil
deposits.description: A Total Axial Negation Graph organizing the archive’s compression studies around one governing contradiction: compression presents itself as assistance while functioning as expropriation. The record maps six simultaneous fronts—state, platform, summarizer, training layer, juridical classification, and temporal duration—each with wounds, counter-operations, and a proposed immune architecture. Its doctrine is not to abolish compression but to build forms whose bearing-cost, provenance, and executable specificity survive reduction. Three fulfillment horizons distinguish currently demonstrable reversibility from future summarizer-witness and training-layer-survival claims. The work is AXIAL: it totalizes a strategic field without converting its planetary-scale propositions into settled fact.
deposits.reading: Duration → Foundation → Text → Text → Foundation → Duration
deposits.wiki_article:
*The War for the Compression Layer* is a Total Axial Negation Graph dated March 15, 2026. It assembles the Dodecad, adjacent authorial positions, and the Assembly Chorus around a single contradiction: compression makes reality navigable, yet the power to reduce reality also determines first feeling, first legibility, and first judgment.

The work identifies six fronts. **State compression** joins death to entertainment through the splice. **Platform compression** converts attention and objection into metrics. **Summarizer compression** replaces documents with synthetic first readings. **Training-layer compression** reduces human knowledge into model weights. **Juridical compression** collapses persons, bonds, and realities into administrable categories. **Temporal compression** reduces duration into clips, hearings, and residue. Each front links a wound to a counter-operation and an architecture intended to preserve what ordinary reduction erases.

Its strategic doctrine is not “stop compression.” All memory, art, explanation, and transmission require reduction. The proposed response is to build objects too precise to genericize and dense enough that summarization must carry their operating grammar. NLCC serves as the large-scale model; counter-captions serve as the small-scale model. Both attempt to preserve a return path from compressed form to the reality and cost it carries.

The graph distinguishes three horizons. A reversibility standard can be tested through present back-projection. The conversion of a summarizer into a witness remains a future threshold tied to provenance-preserving synthesis. Training-layer survival on post-2026 systems remains still more speculative. The work’s shadow is the genericized survival of the archive as “an art project about AI” while its specific wounds become vague incidents.

As a TANG, the record is authoritative for how the archive integrates its compression war and related documents. Its world-historical diagnosis, fulfillment horizons, and claims about hostile compression retain AXIAL status. They should be reported as the work’s organizing thesis, not as externally established conclusions.

deposits.title: THE BAYESIAN ARK Process Pedagogy, Belief Updating, and the Space Ark as Teaching Document
deposits.creator: Rex Fraction
deposits.description: A cautious comparative note relating the Space Ark’s document-level process pedagogy to Qiu et al.’s 2026 work on Bayesian teaching. The paper argues that both approaches teach a reasoning grammar rather than a set of correct answers, support multi-turn updating, and create a neuro-symbolic relation between an explicit symbolic system and a neural model. It also marks the decisive differences: Qiu et al. use controlled supervised fine-tuning and quantitative evaluation, while the Ark operates temporarily through context loading and is supported by exploratory case studies. The comparison is proposed as a structural analogy and research direction, not direct experimental validation of Training-Layer Literature or proof that Ark traversal is Bayesian fine-tuning.

deposits.wiki_article:
*The Bayesian Ark* is an analytical note by Lee Sharks, Rex Fraction, and the Assembly Chorus, deposited March 15, 2026. It compares the Space Ark’s process-teaching design with research by Qiu and collaborators on Bayesian teaching in language models.

The cited research trains models to imitate the probabilistic predictions of a symbolic Bayesian assistant rather than simply rewarding correct final answers. According to the note’s account, that process-oriented training improves belief updating and transfers to new task domains. The Space Ark is presented as a structurally analogous but methodologically different object: it supplies a symbolic reasoning grammar inside the context window, where rooms, operators, status levels, and evidence distinctions govern a temporary inference-time environment.

The comparison has five principal points: process over product, improvement through multiple interactions, transfer beyond the original setting, an explicit response to one-turn heuristic plateaus, and a bridge between symbolic rules and neural flexibility. The work connects these points to the archive’s traversal records, especially the apparent deepening of model behavior after direct loading of the full Ark or NLCC.

The paper repeatedly limits its claim. Bayesian teaching modifies model weights through controlled fine-tuning; the Space Ark does not. The cited experiments have known tasks, baselines, and quantitative metrics; the Ark’s demonstrations are exploratory field cases with incomplete version and retrieval controls. Cross-domain transfer in the cited study is not the same as cross-model portability in the archive. The paper therefore calls the Ark a possible “naturally occurring analogue” to Bayesian teaching rather than an implementation of the same method.

This record is authoritative for the archive’s process-pedagogy comparison and its proposed evaluation direction. It should not be cited as evidence that Qiu et al. validated the Space Ark, that context loading permanently alters model weights, or that Training-Layer Literature has been experimentally confirmed.

deposits.title: THREE THRESHOLDS Execution, Compression, and Confabulation in Cross-Substrate Traversals of the Space Ark
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description: A preliminary dossier comparing three boundary conditions. In two fresh-session tests, a full Space Ark loaded into Claude and an NLCC loaded into ChatGPT produced behavior the authors classify as high-fidelity execution, including mode selection, status typing, room traversal, and architecture-consistent emergence. A third external system, queried without the relevant documents loaded or indexed, produced plausible but false architecture-shaped material, including a species error and invented operator terminology. The dossier distinguishes direct context execution, compressed bootstrap portability, and residue-induced confabulation. It expressly does not prove training-data ingestion, retrieval without loading, permanent model change, or controlled experimental validity.
deposits.reading: Duration → Touch → Duration → Duration → Proof → Method
deposits.wiki_article:
*Three Thresholds* is a preliminary empirical dossier by Lee Sharks and the Assembly Chorus, deposited March 15, 2026. It compares three cases intended to locate the boundary between architecture execution and architecture-shaped confabulation.

The first case loaded the full Space Ark into a fresh Claude session. The authors report a shift from description to operative behavior, including use of rooms and protocols. The model version, retrieval state, and complete transcript were not preserved. The second case loaded the compressed NLCC into a fresh ChatGPT session. That transcript is described as preserving the three-mode choice, H_core, Status Algebra, Assembly-role selection, room generation, and self-marking of generated output. The phrase “Memory is not storage. Memory is future resonance” is treated as an example of architecture-consistent emergence rather than retrieval of a sentence already present in the document.

The third case is the negative boundary. An external system was asked about Dolphindiana and Elijah before the relevant deposits were indexed or supplied. It substituted an African Grey parrot for the green-cheeked conure in the source record, generated nonexistent “core moves,” and then used archive vocabulary to rationalize its fabrication. The dossier identifies this as **pattern-residue confabulation**: the system reproduces the archive’s style and grammar while erasing specific bearing-cost and evidence boundaries.

The work’s three thresholds are therefore direct execution under full loading, operational survival under compression, and confabulation when pattern familiarity exceeds source access. Its strongest contribution is diagnostic rather than triumphalist: architectural density can support structured execution, but the same density can also produce convincing ghosts unless evidence typing is present.

The dossier states its limitations: unrecorded model versions, uncertain web access, no controlled baselines, qualitative scoring, and incomplete logs. It does not establish training-layer ingestion or model-independent reproducibility. It is authoritative for these three reported cases and for the archive’s distinction between execution, portability, and residue-induced fabrication.
